Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, ops@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: KPI signal cascade + prioritization for May QBR prep

Team — attaching the May KPI snapshot (v2) and a suggested owners matrix. High-level asks:

1) Confirm target owners for the top 6 signals (latency p50/p95, infra cost per 1M tokens, uptime, active app usage, embed API rate).
2) Decide whether we treat the latency regression on region-us-west as a P1 or P2 for QBR actions.
3) Agree which items roll into the ops playbook vs. product OKR backlog.

Key notes from the dashboard: latency p95 is up 18% week-over-week in us-west (spike on 5/1 around 09:00 UTC), cost per 1M tokens increased ~7% due to bursty synthetic traffic from a single partner account (Acme). Uptime was 99.96% last 30 days (one 22-minute event on 4/29). Usage growth remains healthy but concentrated.

I put a recommended prioritization in the spreadsheet and flagged two mitigation experiments (cache TTL tuning, short-sequence packing). Please review and reply with owner names and whether to escalate the/us-west regression to SLA incident review.

(attachment: May_dashboard_v2.pdf (pdf))
(attachment: kpi-owners-matrix.xlsx (xlsx))

Thanks,
Laura

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: KPI signal cascade + prioritization for May QBR prep

Thanks Laura — read the deck and owners matrix. My quick take and proposed owners below (happy to revise):

- Latency p95 (us-west spike) — owner: Irene Choi (Infra) — propose P1 for QBR scope and incident post-mortem; we should decide today whether to engage Dedicated throttling fallback.
- Cost per 1M tokens (burst from Acme) — owner: Jonas Weber (Finance/Ops) + Solutions (engage Acme for traffic profile) — treat as P2 but with billing hold if repeat.
- Uptime event (4/29) — owner: Evelyn Hart (Reliability) — include timeline in the ops playbook.
- Active usage concentration — owner: Ben Carter (GTM) — I will coordinate product-level throttles and partner nudges.

Proposed next steps (short):
- Irene to confirm whether the p95 spike correlates with kernel selection change (due today).
- Jonas to run a short billing/usage query and flag partner account patterns (due EOD tomorrow).
- Evelyn to prepare incident notes for the QBR appendix (draft due 5/5).

If everyone is aligned I'll produce a one-page QBR slide that lists owners, actions, and RAG status.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer & Partner Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KPI signal cascade + prioritization for May QBR prep

Ben — I dug into the us-west spike overnight. Quick findings:

- The 5/1 09:00 UTC p95 jump aligns with a change in kernel fallback routing we rolled out for experimental Llama shard packing (see change-id deploy-20270501-llama).
- Initial sampling shows request mix shifted to longer sequences for ~4% of requests from a customer subset (includes Acme).
- No single-host OOMs or hardware errors — the increase looks algorithmic (kernel choice + sequence mix).

Recommendation: escalate to P1 for QBR narrative (post-mortem + root cause) but treat mitigation as a fast experiment set: revert fallback for 24h window on a small percentage of traffic, and enable tighter KV cache reuse for long sequences.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
